parking_rules.summary: When the mayor declares a snow emergency, wintertime alternate-side parking starts: park on the even-numbered side from 7 AM on even dates to 7 AM the next day, and on the odd-numbered side on odd dates. parking_rules.quote: Alternate side of the street parking shall mean that vehicles shall be allowed to stand or park on the even-numbered side of the street between the hours of seven a.m. (7:00am) of the day bearing an even-numbered calendar date to seven a.m. (7:00am) of the following day

safety.geography: Jersey City Police Department: serves Jersey City city, population 305,000
safety.basis: citywide police rate for Jersey City: the same figure for every Jersey City neighborhood, not a rate for Greenville

subcity_estimate.label: 10-month estimate from the city's incident portal, not an official rate
subcity_estimate.method: JC IMPACT block-geocoded incident points counted inside each neighborhood polygon; annualised by 365/days; divided by ACS 2019-2023 resident population of the neighborhood's tracts; 'scaled_to_fbi' = ratio to the citywide portal rate x the FBI agency rate. NOT the FBI agency rate and not comparable with NYPD precinct rates without that scaling

parking_rules.summary: Many Jersey City streets are zone-permit streets: without a resident zone permit you can park at most 2 hours where signs say so.
parking_rules.quote: Resident parking permits are required for parking for more than 2 hours in many areas.

parking_rules.summary: To get or renew a zone permit the driver's license must show the Jersey City home address and the registration must be valid; renewals are reviewed by hand each time. The page states no fee and no building-size exclusion.
parking_rules.quote: Driver's License: Must be valid and reflect your current residential address.

parking_rules.summary: Street-cleaning no-parking times are set block by block on posted signs. When the city suspends parking regulations, street cleaning, zone-permit and meter rules are not enforced that day.
parking_rules.quote: Posted signs will indicate a need for a parking permit, parking restrictions for street cleaning, and other limitations for street parking.

parking_rules.summary: In a snow emergency all cars must be moved off the designated snow emergency routes (city ordinance 332-34); violators are ticketed and towed.
parking_rules.quote: Remove all vehicles from designated snow EMERGENCY ROUTES to facilitate plowing/salting operations.

dog_rules.summary: Every dog 6 months or older needs a Jersey City license and must wear the tag in public; license at the shelter or online.
dog_rules.quote: NJ law requires a license for all dogs 6 months or older. Dogs must wear their license tag when in public.

dog_rules.summary: 2026 fees: 1 year $10 neutered / $20 unneutered; 3 years $25 / $50; $5 late fee after June 30. Rabies vaccination proof required.
dog_rules.quote: Neutered dogs: $10.00 per dog Unneutered dogs: $20.00 per dog

dog_rules.summary: Statewide: dogs 7 months or older must be licensed every year through the town where the owner lives, with proof of rabies vaccination. Town fees run $1.50 to $21 per dog, plus $1 state fee and $3 more if not spayed/neutered.
dog_rules.quote: Dogs seven months of age or older must be licensed annually through the municipality where the owner lives.

voices.excerpt: We came on a whim to liberty harbor community. they have the best events and really incorporate community values for all.with 2 littles under 2, we feel safe and comfortable walking at any hour in the night.
Super dog friendly and lots of wide parks for seeking space. we were beyond lucky to live here.
Growing up in Greenville I grew up in a much more low-income area in comparison to some other locations like Downtown.
voices.context: former resident; says grew up / lifelong there

voices.excerpt: Overall living there has been so peaceful and good to me and my family.
The cost of living here in Jersey City has also increased by a lot. Rent has become unaffordable for low to moderate income families.
I have been living here since I can remember, things have changed yet the feeling home is always there. The beauty sunsets and sunrises to the lovely neighbors and street cats.

I appreciate the convenient access to public transportation such as the NJ Transit buses, light rail and the PATH train from Jersey City to New York City, and towards Penn Station, making it comfortable for a resident to explore the location without a car.
The food scene is amazing with cuisines from around the world. The waterfront areas are beautiful and well maintained.
As someone who has lived here for 17+ years it’s been so nice to meet new people, see new things, and just enjoy my surroundings in this area.
voices.context: current resident; says lived there 17+ years

voices.excerpt: I could see Manhattan from my apartment which was kind of cool, but mainly I liked that I could get into the city in like 20 minutes on the PATH without paying Manhattan rent.
I love how there's public transportation, not having a car isn't a home sentence. I do wish there were more stops or lines on the PATH or Hudson-Bergen Light Rail.
voices.context: current resident; says grew up / lifelong there

voices.excerpt: I do believe that it is less safe than some other cities but honestly, no where in America is completely safe.
Another major concern is the lack of adequate parking. Finding a parking space is consistently frustrating and inconvenient, especially when returning home after a long day.
That being said, there is obvious growth, and the people are doing their best with what they have. It has a lot of opportunity, beautiful architecture, and nice parks.
But there are select few places that will move you, like views downtown during a sunset. I love the city skyline downtown, I also love the food and cultural diversity.
There were moments when the city felt loud and intimidating, and adjusting to a new environment wasn’t easy.
Similar to NYC, without all the crowdedness and expensive prices.

Being a resident here since I was little, I was able to find a community within my own home, one that provides fun and an abundance of shared laughs whilst also making sure people get the education needed.

For the amount of money residents pay, basic expectations such as a clean, odor-free environment and reasonable parking accommodations should be met. I would not recommend living here based on my experience.
I love my city for how convenient it is everything is 15 minutes to 1 hour away from Major cities like NYC or Philly.
As a young woman, walking around alone often feels unsafe and anxiety-inducing—I almost never do it.
What I really like about Newark is its diversity—you can meet people from all over the world, and that brings a lot of culture, different perspectives, and good food!
It very hectic in the morning times and calm during the night.
I hope that in the future, this problem is solved and my community is much better.

There are plenty of outdoor spaces, plenty of parks and playgrounds. We have a community YMCA and a community pool.

The vibrant arts scene, especially the Union County Performing Arts Center, always made the downtown feel alive, and the local restaurants offered a mix of flavors that reflected the community’s diversity.
Rahway is a peaceful town, full of color, and kind-hearted people. The citizens of Rahway are very welcoming and accept everyone with open arms.
Rahway is one of those towns that care deeply about the experience of their residents.
The train station in the heart of town made it so easy to connect to New York City, yet Rahway itself had enough character to make you proud to call it home.
Also, the crime rate is not high, the schools are good, and the social life is good. Downtown Rahway has many well-known restaurants and stores.
I like all the restaurants and mini-stores near downtown and I love Rahway River park. I would like to see the parking situation change.

parking_rules.summary: Many NYC streets have alternate side parking (ASP) for street cleaning; days and hours are on the signs for each block. You cannot park on the side being cleaned for the whole posted time, even after the sweeper has passed.
parking_rules.quote: You cannot park on the side of the street that is being cleaned when ASP rules are in effect. The rules apply for the length of the entire block, and for the entire time posted on the sign, even if the street sweeper has already passed.

parking_rules.summary: ASP is not in effect on Sundays, and is suspended on listed legal and religious holidays, in severe weather and in emergencies.
parking_rules.quote: ASP rules are suspended on certain legal and religious holidays each year, during severe weather, and for emergencies. On Sundays, ASP is not in effect

parking_rules.summary: The city may suspend ASP for snow or emergencies, sometimes announced late in the day; ASP is restored after a snowfall so plows can clear the curb lane. No citywide snow-route parking ban was found on the pages read.
parking_rules.quote: NYC may suspend ASP regulations because of inclement weather or emergencies. The decision is sometimes made late in the day since weather patterns can change fast. NYC restores ASP regulations after a snowfall.

parking_rules.summary: No citywide overnight street-parking ban appears on NYC DOT's parking pages; what applies is whatever the signs on the block say, and the most restrictive sign wins.
parking_rules.quote: If there is more than one sign posted for the same area, the more restrictive one is the one in effect. If a sign is missing on a block, the remaining posted regulations are the ones that are in effect. Please check the entire block and read all signs carefully before you park.

parking_rules.summary: All of NYC is a tow-away zone: a car parked illegally, or with a missing or expired registration or inspection sticker, may be towed.
parking_rules.quote: All of New York City is a designated Tow Away Zone under the State's Vehicle and Traffic Law. This means that any vehicle parked or operated illegally, or with missing or expired registration or inspection stickers, may be towed.

parking_rules.summary: Parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant is illegal.
parking_rules.quote: It is illegal to park within 15 feet of either side of a fire hydrant

parking_rules.summary: Meters are not in effect on Sundays or on the six major legal holidays. Other hours are on the meter or sign.
parking_rules.quote: Metered regulations are not in effect on Sundays nor major legal holidays (New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day).

parking_rules.summary: Passenger meter rates outside Manhattan's core: $2.50 first hour and $5.00 second hour in business districts such as Downtown Flushing and Jamaica; $2.00 / $3.00 in neighborhood retail districts; $1.50 / $2.50 elsewhere.
parking_rules.quote: Zone 1 - Business Districts outside of Manhattan (e.g., Downtown Brooklyn, Downtown Flushing, and Jamaica; Manhattan 125th Street) $2.50 $5.00 Zone 2 - Neighborhood Retail Districts $2.00 $3.00 Zone 3 - All Other Metered Locations $1.50 $2.50

parking_rules.summary: NYC DOT garages sell monthly permits: Court Square (Queens) $400, Borough Hall (Brooklyn) $330, Bay Ridge $275, Jerome-190th Street (Bronx) $250, Delancey and Essex (Manhattan) $600. No monthly rate is listed for the Queens Family Court garage in Jamaica.
Monthly garage permits are reserved online, first come first served, from five days before the month starts; a New York State driver's license check is run at reservation.
parking_rules.quote: Reservations open on the website five days before the first of the month at 10 am. All reservations are made for the upcoming month, on a first-come, first-served basis. A New York State Department of Motor Vehicles driver's license check is performed at the time of the reservation.

parking_rules.summary: Municipal parking fields (open lots) do not allow overnight parking; they close at the posted hour, typically 10 PM.
parking_rules.quote: Municipal parking fields do not allow overnight parking. The fields close as shown in the posted regulations for each facility. Parking after posted hours may result in a summons and leaves the vehicle at risk as there is no security at the closed facilities.

parking_rules.summary: Quarterly permits at municipal parking fields: Flushing #4 $300, Steinway #1 (Astoria) $500, Bayside $500, Brighton Beach $625, Sheepshead Bay #1 $300, Canarsie $300, Bronxdale $400.
parking_rules.quote: Bronxdale Municipal Parking Field $400 Bensonhurst #1 Municipal Parking Field $300 Brighton Beach Municipal Parking Field $625 Canarsie Municipal Parking Field $300 Sheepshead Bay #1 Municipal Parking Field $300 Bayside Municipal Parking Field $500 Flushing #4 Municipal Parking Field $300 Steinway #1 Municipal Parking Field $500

dog_rules.summary: Every dog in NYC must be licensed and wear the tag in public. A license costs $8.50 a year for a spayed or neutered dog; $34 for an unaltered dog over 4 months.
dog_rules.quote: All dogs in New York City must have licenses, and the licenses must be attached to their collars while in public.

dog_rules.summary: License fee: $8.50 a year if spayed or neutered; if not, $8.50 under 4 months old and $34 over 4 months.
dog_rules.quote: Licenses for spayed or neutered dogs of any age cost $8.50 per year. If your dog is not spayed or neutered, a license will cost $8.50 if the dog is under 4 months old, or $34 if it is older than 4 months.

dog_rules.summary: In any public place a dog must be on a leash no longer than six feet.
dog_rules.quote: a person who owns, possesses or controls a dog shall not permit it to be in any public place or in any open or unfenced area abutting on a public place unless the dog is effectively restrained by a leash or other restraint not more than six feet long.

dog_rules.summary: In city parks dogs must be leashed except where Parks rules allow off-leash; the Health Code lets Parks allow off-leash in unenclosed areas only within a window that starts no earlier than 9 PM and ends by 9 AM. The Parks rules themselves could not be read (site bot-walled).
dog_rules.quote: Such rules shall include provisions that prohibit unrestrained dogs in unenclosed DOPR controlled areas and facilities except during a specified range of time, that shall not begin earlier than 9:00 P.M. and not extend past 9:00 A.M.

dog_rules.summary: With proof of a current license and rabies vaccination, dogs can run off-leash in NYC Parks dog runs. The open-data list has 95 active runs (14 in Queens, 20 Brooklyn, 41 Manhattan, 15 Bronx, 5 Staten Island); see dog_parks.csv.
dog_rules.quote: With proof of current dog license and rabies vaccination, dogs can run off-leash at New York City park dog runs

dog_rules.summary: Owners must pick up after their dog in all public areas; the fine is up to $250.
dog_rules.quote: If you do not clean up after your dog, you may be fined up to $250.

voices.excerpt: I wish there was more diversity, more nightlights for when going home late and also more safety. At night, it’s very scary to walk home alone as a women.
There are also various parks throughout the neighborhood, Bryant park being a well known neighborhood park.

The subway station is situated in an area surrounded by cafe’s, restaurants, grocery stores, hair salons&boutiques.This makes it easy for locals to grab a bite of food or do some quick shopping before/after riding the train.
Great community with a peaceful environment in the DAY.

Buying is pricey — expect $800k+, especially for multifamily properties. It's a solid choice if you're starting out in NYC and great for families looking for space, rental affordability, and local convenience.
How it provides a family-friendly environment as well as a multicultural neighborhood where families of different cultures live.
Another way of transit is the train, Sheepshead Bay is connected to the B and the Q train. These transportation connects to many other lines that allow an easy and smooth transfer.
It feels safe most of the time, it is mostly residential and quiet at night. Diverse residents.
Sheepshead Bay is a diverse, urban neighborhood with strong public schools, is very family-friendly, and has easy access to the beach, Coney Island, and Marine Park for sports and playdates.

Grocery is considered affordable compared to many neighborhoods, there is many fast food chains around the area as well as restaurants for dining. The people are very friendly, though it is not as diverse as other neighborhoods in the upper north.
There is 3 buses and 2 trains that come to Sheapshead bay along with an highway exit. House rents vary from 1,500 to 3,000 It all depends on your preferences and income.
When it comes to transportation, The B and Q trains are the ones that take you to the neighborhood. Some buses that run are the B36, B44, B4, and B49.

voices.excerpt: Yonkers is a moderately safe city depending on which county you're in, but not many crimes or large incidents occur here. My neighborhood is pretty safe and the people are welcoming and friendly.
There’s plenty to do from walking a trail, getting out for a run or bike ride, sitting at the park and looking at the water, and visiting the Utermeyer Garden.
However, I am a female and I have been approached by random men on multiple occasions which has made me feel uncomfortable with going out alone, but there's nothing you can really do about that.
It's normally calm and quiet, with very few disturbances.
I appreciate that Yonkers is a very diverse community where people are generally friendly and welcoming.
There's so much coming to Yonkers, but the true hidden gems are the small local spots that are filled with culture and work ethic.
I would like to see fixes in the roads, fixes in the traffic, and cleaning up the streets in the areas near the library in South Yonkers.

There is the right balance of entertainment and also quiet in the area.

These challenges have motivated me to pursue higher education and seek ways to contribute back to my community, especially through initiatives that promote educational equity and community development.

host.intro: The apartments in Yonkers are by the river, 0.3 miles from the water. Residents praise the trails, parks and views along it. Only 4 restaurants are within a 10-minute walk of most buildings here.

The supermarket is 0.2 miles away.
The nearest dog park is 1.2 miles away.
Your parents are about 36 minutes away by car.
Many households here have no car, so ask each building about parking.
